summary: Vercel's open-source reference app for background coding agents: a developer describes a coding task in a web app, a durable agent plans and edits the code by calling tools, and it works inside a separate sandbox machine with its own files, shell and git. When it finishes it can commit the changes and open a pull request on GitHub.

narrative: A [[developer]] signs in on the [[pages]], picks a repo and describes a coding task in the [[workspace]].
The [[api]] hands the task to the [[agent]], a background worker that plans, reads and edits code by calling tools and asking the [[svc-ai-model]].
The agent never works inside the app itself: it drives a separate [[sandbox]] that holds the files, a shell and git.
When a run succeeds, the [[platform]] commits the changes and can open a pull request through [[svc-github]].
[[svc-postgres]] keeps sessions, chats and usage, and [[svc-redis]] keeps each person under their rate limit.
A [[teammate]] can read a shared chat, and [[github]] tells the app when a pull request changes.

tours.title: Giving the agent a task
captions: The chat page wraps everything in a chat context that owns the conversation.
The context starts the chat runtime, which sends each message to the server.
The runtime posts the message to the chat route, which can also resume or stop a run.
The route checks who is asking and starts the background chat run.
The run builds the coding agent and gives it the tools and the sandbox.
The agent asks the AI model what to do next, and keeps calling tools until the task is done.

tours.title: Starting a sandbox
captions: Creating a session also asks for a sandbox to be built for it.
The kick-off helper starts the provisioning workflow so the request can return at once.
The workflow does the slow work in the background, step by step.
Provisioning builds the sandbox and needs access to the repo before it can clone it.
The access check finds a GitHub token the app may use for this repo.
The GitHub client asks the GitHub API for the repo and its permissions.

tours.title: Committing the work
captions: When the run ends, the chat run hands over to its finish step.
If the developer turned auto-commit on, the finish step commits the sandbox's changes.
The commit step asks the git helpers for the changes and a commit message.
The helpers ask the AI model to write a message that describes the change.

tours.title: Opening a pull request
captions: The create-PR dialog collects the title and description and calls a server action.
The action checks the session, pushes the branch from the sandbox and opens the pull request.
The pull request helpers build the request to GitHub.
The GitHub client sends it to the GitHub API.
